problem: REVERIE / REVERIE-CE evaluation inherits the VLN-CE 3 m success criterion around an annotated endpoint, ignoring final heading and target visibility. Agents can count as successful while not near, or not facing, the referred object instance (the Last-3-Meter Grounding Gap).
motivation: Downstream inspection or manipulation needs a final viewpoint where the referred object is visible and localizable, not just region arrival. ETPNav-FT gets 34.67% SR but only 6.32% ONS@0.1m and 11.31% OracleGS, so strong SR does not imply instance-level grounding.
key_idea: Decouple fine-grained final approach from long-horizon navigation with a plug-and-play, LoRA-finetuned UniNaVid refinement policy trained with a visibility-aware stop penalty, followed by phrase extraction and OWLv2 grounding, evaluated with new instance-centric metrics on REVERIE-AIM.
insight: A short-horizon RGB-only refiner trained on 180K approach clips improves every one of four very different upstream policies, so the last-3-meter deficit is separable from upstream navigation quality. Removing the visibility-aware stop penalty (Ours w/o VSP) consistently lowers ONS and OracleGS, e.g. ONS@0.1m 14.96 -> 12.43 on UniNavid-ZS, showing premature stopping is a key failure mode. The gap to human performance (25.89 vs 74.71 ONS@0.5m) stays large.
method: Three-stage pipeline: upstream policy navigates until stop; refinement policy pi_ref repositions and reorients; then grounding module predicts the box on the final view.

Refinement policy: UniNaVid (video VLA) with LoRA on all LLM linear layers and a frozen vision encoder; input is egocentric RGB video plus instruction; predicts 4-step action sequences over {forward, turn_left, turn_right, stop}.

Visibility-Aware Stop Penalty: stop margin m = z_stop - max other logit at the first action token; L_vsp = mean of ReLU(m) over target-invisible samples (visibility from simulator annotations); L_total = L_CE + lambda_vsp * L_vsp.

Target extraction and grounding: BERT-Large extractive QA (fine-tuned on 2,048 GPT-4o-mini-annotated instruction-phrase pairs) extracts the target phrase; OWLv2 uses it as text query for the bounding box.

REVERIE-AIM dataset: REVERIE trajectories remapped to Habitat continuous space; endpoints replaced by ObjectNav instance-level sampling points (mean min geodesic distance to target 1.32 m -> 0.34 m); 3,691 train trajectories (53 scenes, 90 categories), 1,344 val-unseen trajectories (10 scenes, 48 categories).

Short-horizon data: start from the second-to-last reference node, with Gaussian position perturbation (sigma 1.5, truncated to ±5 m) and random heading in [-pi, pi]; shortest-path expert actions give about 180K clips.
Metrics: ONS@tau (geodesic distance to navigable points around the target instance, tau 0.1/0.5 m), GS (IoU>=0.5 of the predicted box), OracleGS (GT box visible and >=1% of frame area).

setting.backbone: UniNaVid (LoRA-finetuned) refiner + BERT-Large QA + OWLv2 detector; upstream ETPNav-ZS/FT, UniNaVid-ZS, SmartWay
setting.model_size: UniNaVid (7B-class VLA; size not stated in paper); BERT-Large
setting.training_data: About 180K short-horizon approach samples from REVERIE-AIM train (3,691 trajectories); 2,048 instruction-phrase pairs for the BERT extractor
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB only (refiner); no depth, map or upstream changes
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes) plus a real Hello Robot Stretch
setting.privileged: none at test time (visibility annotations used only in training loss); metrics use GT annotations

numbers.extra: refiner trained on 180K REVERIE-AIM clips; upstream SR 28.94

numbers.eval_set_note: 12 real-world episodes in a robot lab, lobby and foyer
numbers.extra: real robot; ONS@0.5m defined by Euclidean distance
numbers.evidence: Table 2, Comparison on Real-world robot evaluation

numbers_note: Own baselines and no-refinement rows are omitted; standard R2R-style metrics (SR/SPL/NE) are only given for upstream backbones, not for REALM.
results: REALM improves ONS, GS and OracleGS over no-move, random, heuristic CLIP-search and vanilla UniNaVid on all four backbones, e.g. ETPNav-ZS ONS@0.1m 7.07 -> 14.66 and SmartWay OracleGS 4.69 -> 15.92. On the real robot ONS@0.5m rises from 8.33 to 33.33. Human eval remains far higher (ONS@0.5m 74.71).
limitations: Absolute performance remains far below the human upper bound (ONS@0.5m 25.89 vs 74.71).
Refinement is only short-horizon motion; it lacks active viewpoint selection and visibility reasoning, and GS is very low (under 9%).
Real-world evaluation is tiny (12 episodes); the benchmark is derived from REVERIE-CE and covers only val-unseen in simulation.
